title: Claude fallback implementer: shell rules in the brief, one automatic report nudge, a short denied count in status
lead: When the Claude implementer (matrix row r3) stands in for Codex, ork gives it three fixes. Its brief says which shell commands it may use and how (Claude only). A report with a shape error gets one automatic nudge to the same session before the run pauses. `ork status` shows a short count of denied commands instead of their text.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Wave 5 (2026-11-02, owner's report of S238 and S190, which ork ran): Codex was out of credits at launch, ork fell back to the Claude implementer (matrix row r3, claude sonnet high), and both runs paused with `report shape: no "Tests: N passed, M failed" line; no "## Owner needed" section; next: ork retry RUN`. The status line then printed the denied Bash commands. The owner decided on 2026-11-02 (interactive) that this goes in pass v1.1 and chose three parts, called option (3): (a) shell rules for the Claude implementer, (b) one automatic nudge on a report shape pause, (c) a short denied count in status. Whether ork should hold an engine-slice run until Codex's out-until time instead of falling back to Claude is not decided and is not part of this slice.

What the code at HEAD of main shows (verified 2026-11-02):

- The Claude implementer runs on an allowlist. `DefaultImplementerAllowlist` (`internal/engine/perm.go:24-36`) holds `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `Edit`, `Write` and prefix patterns such as `Bash(slicer *)`, `Bash(go -C * test*)`, `Bash(gofmt *)`, plus `Bash(<check command>*)`. It has no `sed`, `python3`, `cd`, `grep` or `rg` entry. A registry `permissions.implementer` list replaces the default as is (`ResolvePermission`, `perm.go:47-69`; `TestImplementerGetsTheRegistryAllowlistAsIs`). The Claude adapter passes the list as `--allowedTools a,b --permission-prompts none` (`internal/agent/claude/args.go:46-59`), and Codex gets `workspace-write` or `read-only` instead (`internal/agent/codex/codex.go:53-56`). So a `sed -i`, a `python3` heredoc or a `cd X && ...` command matches no default pattern, and it is denied for Claude and runs for Codex.
- The brief does not list the allowlist. `BriefInput` (`internal/engine/brief.go:20-35`) has no allowlist field, and `runRound` builds it at `internal/engine/round.go:261-270` without `perm.Allow`. `ork run` prints the allowlist (`internal/cli/run.go:200`), but the role never sees it.
- The role prompt is one file for every vendor. `roles.Prompt(name)` takes no vendor (`internal/roles/roles.go:43-53`), and `internal/roles/prompts/implementer.md` is embedded and canonical (`roles.prompts`, adj 29). `TestNoClaudeCodeOnlyMechanics` (`internal/roles/roles_test.go:207`) forbids the word Bash in a prompt. The brief builder already branches on the vendor (`brief.go:81`, the UI pass skills line). So a Claude-only line belongs in `BuildBrief`, and `implementer.md` stays as it is (Codex unchanged).
- A shape error pauses at once. `CheckReport` (`internal/engine/report.go:114-174`) collects the problems; `runRound` pauses with `Pending{Kind: PendingShape}` when any exist (`internal/engine/round.go:489-494`). `ork retry RUN` reruns the role and resumes its session, with a `## Report shape` section naming the problems (`pendingSection`, `round.go:135-136`; resume allowed at `round.go:251-255`). The round limit counts implementer fix rounds only (`bumpRound`, `internal/engine/states.go:132-142`; `DefaultMaxRounds` 8, `internal/engine/engine.go:26`). A retry of a shape pause stays in the same round and writes `ROLE-N-attempt-M.md` (`round.go:225-234`). The spec check already reruns once on a shape error, in its own code path (`RunSpecCheck`, `internal/engine/speccheck.go:145-154`); this slice does not touch it.
- The status line prints at most three denials in full and then `and N more` (`source.DenialsText`, `internal/source/source.go:267-273`; used at `internal/cli/daemoncmds.go:88-90`). Each denial text is `Tool: command` capped at 200 characters (`internal/agent/claude/types.go:74,82-101`; `internal/runrec/record.go:73-88`), so three Bash denials can fill several lines. The daemon builds `EngineRun.Denials` as distinct texts in first-seen order with ` xN` for repeats (`internal/daemon/runs.go:1287-1303`, field at `internal/source/source.go:260`). The TUI uses the same `DenialsText` (`internal/tui/overview.go:386,987`).

Not verified (the run logs are outside the workspace and were not read):

- Why the two final reports lacked the shape. A report file that is missing or empty falls back to the vendor's final message text (`readReport`, `round.go:577-592`), which would lack both parts; that is consistent with what happened but not shown.
- Which exact commands Sonnet was denied. The five kinds the owner named (a `python3` heredoc edit, `sed -i` on a Go file, `grep` into `sed`, `cd` then `sed`, `rg` pipelines) match no default pattern, as above. Whether the ork project's registry entry holds `Bash(rg *)` is not shown in the workspace; the default list has no `rg`.
- That Claude Code's matcher refuses a pipe, `cd`, a heredoc or `sed -i` after an allowed prefix. That is Claude Code's behaviour, not ork's; the repo's fixtures show only a denied `Write` (`testdata/vendors/claude/04-allowlist-denies-write.stdout`).
- The status line printing "every" command. At HEAD it prints at most three, each up to 200 characters, then a count.

Design choices (*proposed* until an adj record decides them; the owner has not answered these):

- The shell rules are a section of the Claude implementer's brief, built from the allowlist the role really has, not text in the shared prompt.
- The nudge applies to every role round that goes through `runRound` and has a report check: implementer (and its finish step), reviewer, UI pass, gate, architect. The spec check keeps its own retry.
- The nudge reuses the existing `## Report shape` section, which already names every problem. It is not a round (`rec.Round` does not change); it is a second role record in the same round, so its tokens and minutes count toward the run's budgets, and it is skipped when a budget is already reached.
- `ork status` counts distinct denial texts and shows the first one cut to 40 characters. `--json` and the TUI are unchanged.

Owner decisions (interactive question, 2026-11-02): the three parts are the whole slice; the answers stated in this spec are accepted as written (every report-checked role gets the one nudge, it is not a round, and the denied count reads as stated); the spec check keeps its own existing retry (it failed twice on S235 on 2026-11-02, which is why the nudge is worth having elsewhere); ork keeps falling back to the Claude implementer when Codex is out (it does not hold the run). Related owner rule, 2026-11-02: for Grok and any other vendor, do not pin a model version unless the owner asks; default to the vendor's latest.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
Part (a), `internal/engine/brief_test.go`:

- TestClaudeImplementerBriefHasShellRules: `BriefInput{Role: RoleImplementer, Vendor: "claude", Allowlist: DefaultImplementerAllowlist("go test ./...")}`. The brief has a `## Shell commands` section that says to change files with the Edit and Write tools, to run one plain command per shell call, and not to use pipes, `cd`, heredocs, scripts or `sed -i`. It lists every `Bash(...)` entry of the allowlist as the pattern inside the parentheses (`slicer *`, `go -C * test*`, `go test ./...*`) and the other entries as tool names. Fails first: it does not compile, because `BriefInput` has no `Allowlist` field; after the field exists, it fails because there is no section.
- TestShellRulesOnlyForTheClaudeImplementer: no `## Shell commands` section, and a brief equal to the one built without `Allowlist`, for a codex implementer, an empty vendor, `Claude` (case-sensitive), and a claude reviewer, gate, architect, UI pass and spec-check. Fails first: compile error as above (no `Allowlist` field).
- TestShellSectionFollowsTheRegistryAllowlist: a list of `Edit` and `Bash(dotnet test*)` shows `dotnet test*` and `Edit` and none of the default entries (`slicer *` is absent). A list with no `Bash(` entry says the role has no shell commands. A check command with a backtick or newline in its entry stays inside a fence that is longer than any backtick run in it (the rule of `brief.go:94-105`). Fails first: no section.
- TestFinishStepBriefKeepsTheShellSection: with `Finish: true` the section is still present (the finish step runs `slicer` commands). Fails first: no section.

Part (a), `internal/engine/fallback_test.go` or `internal/engine/brief_test.go` (use `fallbackHarness` at `fallback_test.go:81`):

- TestClaudeFallbackBriefListsTheRealAllowlist: codex row exits `ExitOutOfCredits`, the claude row runs. The claude request's brief has `## Shell commands` and every `Bash(...)` pattern of that request's `Allowlist`; the codex request's brief has no such section. Fails first: the section is missing.

Part (b), `internal/engine/nudge_test.go` (new; the helper `badAlways` makes the runner return one bad report for a role on every call):

- TestShapeErrorGetsOneNudgeBeforeThePause: the implementer's report has no Tests line and no Owner needed section on both calls. Exactly two implementer requests; the second has `Resume` equal to the first's session and a brief with `## Report shape`, `Tests: N passed` and `Owner needed`; the run is then paused with `Pending{Kind: PendingShape, Role: "implementer", Round: 1}` whose reason is the second report's problems; two implementer role records, the second with report `implementer-1-attempt-2.md`. Fails first: one request, because the pause comes at once.
- TestNudgeThatFixesTheReportContinues: bad report, then a good one. No pause, `Pending` is nil, the run reaches awaiting-approval, two implementer records, and the run record shows no owner question. Fails first: the run pauses.
- TestNoNudgeLoop: after the pause of the test above, `Retry` runs the role once (three implementer requests in all) and the run pauses on a shape error again with no further nudge (still three). Fails first: with no nudge the same steps give two requests, not three.
- TestNudgeIsNotAFixRound: `h.deps.MaxRounds = 1` (as `approval_test.go:173`); bad report, then good. The run does not stop with "the round limit"; `Snapshot().Round` is 1. Fails first: the run pauses before the check.
- TestNudgeRecordCountsTowardTheBudget: bad report, then good, with `h.cfg.Budgets.Tokens = 1500` and 1000 tokens per round. The two implementer records sum to 2000 tokens, so the reviewer does not start and the run pauses with `PendingBudget` (`requireBudgetPause`, `budget_test.go`). Fails first: one record of 1000 tokens, and the reviewer starts.
- TestNoNudgeWhenTheBudgetIsReached: `h.cfg.Budgets.Tokens = 1000` and 1000 tokens per round, so the budget is reached when the implementer's bad report is read. The run pauses on shape with one implementer request. Fails first: it passes before the change; it is a guard, so say so in the report and mutation-check the budget condition.
- TestNoNudgeAfterARetriedShapePause: `Retry` of a shape pause runs the role with `Pending` kind shape; a bad report pauses without a nudge. Same for a shape pause that rides on a question as `pending.retry` (`pendFor`, `states.go:385-401`). Fails first: guard test; mutation-check the guard.
- TestNoNudgeWhenTheSliceIsAlreadyPausedOrStopped: with the run already paused by a sibling (call `e.pause` first and then `runRound` for a reviewer with a bad report), the reviewer is not rerun and the first pause is kept. Fails first: a second request.
- TestNudgeAppliesToEveryReportCheckedRole: table, subtests per role, each with a bad report then a good one, expecting two requests for that role and no pause: implementer, implementer finish step, reviewer, gate (first line not `VERDICT:`), architect (setup of `TestArchitectShapeErrorPausesAndRetryResumesIt`, `architect_test.go:128`) and UI pass (setup of `uipass_test.go`). Fails first: each pauses after one request.
- TestSpecCheckKeepsItsOwnRetry: the existing `TestCheckRerunsOnceOnAShapeError` (`speccheck_test.go:522`) stays green unchanged.

Part (c), `internal/cli`:

- TestStatusCountsDeniedCommands: five denials, the first a 120-character `Bash: ...` text. `ork status` prints `(denied: 5 commands, first: ` plus the first text cut to 40 characters ending in `...`, then `)`; none of the other four texts appears; the line has no text beyond the cut. Fails first: it prints `A, B, C and 2 more` style text.
- TestStatusDeniedOneCommandIsSingular: one denial of 12 characters prints `(denied: 1 command, first: Write: /x.txt)` with no cut. Fails first: old format.
- TestStatusDeniedCutsOnRunesNotBytes: a first denial with multi-byte characters is cut on a rune boundary (valid UTF-8). Fails first: old format.
- TestStatusJSONKeepsEveryDenial: `ork status --json` prints the daemon's `denials` array exactly as received (five long texts). Fails first: passes today; keep it as a guard for "the data in --json is unchanged".
- The pinned texts in `TestStatusBoundsDenials` (`cli_test.go:1247`), `TestStatusPrintsEngineStateAndWait` (`run_test.go:299`) and `TestStatusSectionsAndNeedsRows` (`run_test.go:310`) change to the new format. `internal/tui` tests and `testdata/golden/engine-denials-100x30.txt` stay byte for byte as they are.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Tests first. Watch each fail for the stated reason before the product code.

Do not touch: `internal/roles/prompts/implementer.md` and every other prompt, `internal/source/source.go` (`DenialsText` stays for the TUI), `internal/tui` and `testdata/golden`, `internal/daemon/runs.go` (the `denials` data and `--json` stay as they are), `internal/engine/speccheck.go`, `internal/engine/perm.go`.

1. Part (a), tests: write the four brief tests and the fallback test. Add the field and the section last.
2. Part (a), product: add `Allowlist []string` to `BriefInput`. In `BuildBrief`, after the "Checks ork runs" block and before the round's own sections, when `in.Role == RoleImplementer && in.Vendor == "claude"` (case-sensitive, as `brief.go:81`), write `## Shell commands`. Text (*proposed*): "ork limits your shell to the commands below. Any other command is denied and does not run. Change files with the Edit and Write tools only: no `sed -i`, no scripts (python or others), no heredocs, no redirects into files. Run one plain command per shell call: no pipes, no `&&` or `;`, no command substitution, no `cd` (use absolute paths, `go -C DIR` and `git -C DIR`). If a command is denied, use an allowed form; do not retry it another way." Then "Tools: " plus the non-Bash entries, and the `Bash(...)` entries as their inner patterns, one per line, in one fenced block (fence length by the rule at `brief.go:94-105`; a trailing `*` means any further text). An allowlist with no Bash entry says the role has no shell commands. Do not rewrite the entries. In `runRound` (`round.go:261-270`) set `Allowlist: perm.Allow`. A read-only role has no list, and the section is not written for it.
3. Part (b), tests: write `nudge_test.go` with the helper `badAlways`. Run the whole engine suite after the product change and fix the existing tests that expected an immediate shape pause (listed under Files) by making the runner return the bad report on the nudge as well; keep each test's intent.
4. Part (b), product, in `runRound` at `round.go:489`: when `len(problems) > 0` and the nudge is allowed, run the same round once more by calling `e.runRound(ctx, r, &runrec.Pending{Kind: runrec.PendingShape, State: r.state, Role: r.role, Round: r.n, Reason: (&ShapeError{Problems: problems}).Error()})` and return its result. That call resumes the role's session (`round.go:251-255`) with the `## Report shape` section (`pendingSection`) and, because its context is a shape pause, it cannot nudge again: a second bad report pauses as today. The nudge is allowed only when all hold: `pend` and every `pend.Retry` in its chain are not of kind `PendingShape`; the run's state is still `r.state` (not paused, not stopped); `e.overBudget` is false for the current record; and `ctx.Err()` is nil. Otherwise pause as today. Write no new pending kind, no new record field and no new round number: the second role record, its `-attempt-2.md` report and its step are the only trace. Add a short comment that the nudge is not a round: `bumpRound` (`states.go:132-142`) is the only place that counts rounds, and a shape retry never calls it.
5. Part (b), docs: add the nudge to `docs/design.md:539-545` (one automatic nudge, the same session, then the pause as before; not a round; subject to the budgets; the spec check keeps its own retry) and mark it *proposed*.
6. Part (c), tests: write the three status tests and the JSON guard; update the three pinned old texts.
7. Part (c), product, in `internal/cli/daemoncmds.go:88-90`: replace `source.DenialsText(r.Denials)` with a small helper in `internal/cli` that prints `(denied: N command[s], first: TEXT)`, where N is `len(r.Denials)` (distinct texts), `TEXT` is `r.Denials[0]` cut to 40 runes (37 runes and `...` when longer). Do not change `source.DenialsText` (the TUI uses it), `EngineRun.Denials`, or `--json`.
8. Part (c), docs: `docs/dashboard.md:655-664` (a sentence: `ork status` prints the count and the first denial cut to 40 characters; `ork status --json` lists every denial; the Overview rows are as before), `docs/state.md:443-448`, and `docs/design.md:589-591`.
9. CHANGELOG, last, so a parallel slice's entry does not conflict: add one entry at the bottom of `## Unreleased` that starts "Claude fallback implementer:" and says: the Claude implementer's brief lists its allowed shell commands and the rules for them (*proposed*); a report with a shape error gets one automatic nudge to the same session before the run pauses, not counted as a round (*proposed*); `ork status` shows a count of denied commands and the first one cut short (*proposed*).
10. Mutation-check each new assertion (remove the vendor condition, the budget guard, the retried-pause guard, the state guard, the 40-character cut) and report which test went red.
11. UI slice: UI pass (r14).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...`; `go vet ./...`; `gofmt -l .`; `slicer check`; `adj lint`.
- `go -C WORKTREE test -race -count=1 ./internal/engine ./internal/cli ./internal/roles ./internal/tui` (the TUI goldens must not change: `git -C WORKTREE status --short testdata/golden` prints nothing).
- `rg -n "Bash" internal/roles/prompts/` prints nothing (the prompts stay vendor-neutral), and `git -C WORKTREE diff --stat -- internal/roles` is empty.
- [HUMAN CHECK] `ork status` in a terminal at 100x30 and 80x24 with a run that has five long denied commands: the denied part is one bounded piece of the run's line (about 70 characters), not several lines of command text.
- [HUMAN CHECK] [AFTER LAND] After the daemon is restarted on the landed build, the next Claude stand-in implementer run (Codex out of credits) is watched once: its brief holds the `## Shell commands` section, a report shape error gets exactly one automatic rerun before any pause, and status shows the short denied count.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch: "Claude fallback implementer: shell rules, one report nudge, short denied count".
